name: Martin Harris
role: Book of Mormon scribe, printing financier, and witness
dateNote: He lost the 116 manuscript pages in June 1828 and became one of the Three Witnesses in June 1829.
importance: A Palmyra farmer, Harris wrote for Joseph Smith in 1828 and then lost the first 116 pages, the loss behind sections 3 and 10. Section 5 promises him a witness, and section 17 names him with the Three Witnesses. Section 19 urges him to pay for printing, and he later sold land to cover the cost. Later revelations send him to Missouri, make him an example of consecration, and place him on the Kirtland high council.
connections: Husband of Lucy Harris, who opposed the Book of Mormon. He worked with Joseph Smith, Oliver Cowdery, David Whitmer, and the members of the United Firm.
reviewNote: Dates, baptism (6 April 1830), witness, land sale (deed 7 April 1831), high council, December 1837 excommunication, 1842 and 1870 rebaptisms, and 1870 move to Utah checked on JSP. The section 19 setting cites a 1829 mortgage; JSP notes the later land sale. The 116 pages come from the section 3 and 10 settings.
